original.description: Three officers of Infanterie-Regiment 24 standing in a cobbled street in field-grey with the Pour le Mérite at the throat — left to right: Hauptmann Hans-Joachim Haupt, Oberstleutnant von Oven (regimental commander), Hauptmann Cordt von Brandis — photographed for Die Woche after the award of the Pour le Mérite for the capture of Fort Douaumont (25 February 1916).
original.photographer: unknown; published by August Scherl Verlag, Berlin
original.archive: Die Woche 1918 Nr. 2 (Scherl) via Wikimedia Commons

caption: Haupt, von Oven and von Brandis of the 24th Brandenburg Infantry, the officers credited with taking Fort Douaumont on 25 February 1916 — though it was Haupt's company, and Pionier-Sergeant Kunze who climbed in first; Brandis wrote the book and got the fame. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a public-domain photograph.
credit: Original photograph: Die Woche 1918 Nr. 2, August Scherl Verlag; public domain (via Wikimedia Commons). Colorization: History Alive, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Provided by Dave 2026-08-22. Belongs to the Phase 3 Verdun zoom-in (epic history-alive-g80) — the 'who really took Douaumont' story (Kunze vs. Haupt vs. Brandis) is a ready-made historiography beat. Also a strong uniforms-and-kit reference for the 1915–16 field-grey.
